F1 Hungarian Grand Prix 2026 event centre – Live updates, reports, results, schedule, weather, preview Editor 22 Jul 2026 4:06 PM F1 Hungarian Grand Prix 2026 event centre – Live updates, reports, results, schedule, weather, preview Here’s our full event centre for the 2026 Hungarian Grand Prix weekend including event schedule, live session times, preview, key storylines, weather information and more ahead of what promises to be a crucial early-summer test. The 2026 drivers’ championship took another twist at the Belgian Grand Prix as George Russell crashed out on the opening lap while Kimi Antonelli claimed another win to extend his points advantage. Can Russell hit back this weekend in Hungary, or will Ferrari step up once again? Hungarian Grand Prix live: Quick access Event preview Full event schedule & results Hungarian Grand Prix live timing Hungarian Grand Prix live updates – Practice 1 – Practice 2 – Practice 3 – Qualifying – Race Weather forecast Predictions Key storylines Conclusions Driver Ratings Winners & Losers Hungarian Grand Prix preview: What to expect The Hungarian Grand Prix serves as the high-stakes final showdown before Formula 1’s mandatory summer shutdown, leaving teams eager to finish the first half of the season on a high note. Often dubbed “Monaco without walls,” the Hungaroring’s tight, 14-turn circuit shifts the focus away from straight-line speed toward maximum downforce and deployment management under hot summer conditions. Track position is critical around this notoriously difficult passing layout, placing immense weight on Saturday’s qualifying session. Meanwhile, teams like McLaren and Aston Martin are debuting crucial upgrade packages, and Red Bull enters with momentum hoping the slower layout plays to its chassis strengths. What time is the 2026 Hungarian Grand Prix? Full schedule and session times The 2026 Hungarian Grand Prix weekend takes place at the Hungaroring as Formula 1 heads to Budapest for a traditional format race weekend. Below is the full session schedule for the Hungarian GP 2026, including local and UK times. Friday, 24 July – Practice sessions Practice 1: 13:30-14:30 (12:30 UK) Practice 2: 17:00-18:00 (18:00 UK) Saturday, 25 July – Final practice and qualifying Practice 3: 12:30-13:30 (11:30 UK) Qualifying: 16:00-17:00 (15:00 UK) Sunday, 26 July – Race day Race: 16:00 (15:00 UK) Hungarian GP weather forecast Warm but not sweltering conditions will prevail through practice and qualifying, but there is a rising chance of rain on Sunday. Check out the full weather forecast for the weekend ahead Key storylines Championship leader Kimi Antonelli arrives in Budapest fresh off his sixth victory of the season at Spa, but Mercedes teammate George Russell’s lap-one battery issue highlighted an ongoing reliability bug that the team must fix before the summer shutdown. Eight-time Hungaroring winner Lewis Hamilton and teammate Charles Leclerc head to a track that heavily favours the high-downforce, medium-speed cornering profile of the Ferrari SF-26, offering Scuderia a good chance to chip away at Mercedes’ championship lead. Aston Martin is bringing a major, single-package update designed by Adrian Newey, featuring a re-homologated lighter chassis, a new nose, and reworked aero as it bids to rescue a troubled start to the new 2026 technical regulations. McLaren is introducing a targeted upgrade package aimed at fixing the MCL40’s low-speed balance issues, hoping to net a podium finish for Lando Norris and Oscar Piastri before the mid-season break. records.evidence: Google News RSSで「レッドブルがマルコの後任を決定か。メルセデスのドライバー育成プログラム責任者ラグリュを獲得へ」を確認し、配信元ページhttps://topics.smt.docomo.ne.jp/article/asweb/sports/asweb-20260722_1336766?page=2を特定した。本文抽出: サッカーW杯 LIVE プロ野球 MLB LIVE ゴルフ 大相撲 LIVE プロ野球（2軍） LIVE テニス 高校野球 競馬 Jリーグ レッドブルがマルコの後任を決定か。メルセデスのドライバー育成プログラム責任者ラグリュを獲得へ 7/22(水) 9:36 share シェア X Facebook LINE 閉じる ラグリュがいつレッドブルへ加わるかは現時点では不明だ。関係者によれば、彼はまだメルセデスへ正式な辞表を提出しておらず、辞職決定後も一定期間のガーデニング休暇を経て初めて新天地へ移ることができる。 スパ・フランコルシャンの週末、ウォルフとラグリュは話し合いを行い、メルセデスの利益を守りつつも、ラグリュの移籍に過度な障害を設けない形で合意に達するための交渉を行った。 ■ラグリュはロケリンと連携して若手発掘に携わる見込み レッドブルでのラグリュの最初の仕事は、育成プログラムに加える新たな有望カートドライバーを発掘・選抜することになるだろう。同時に、すでに育成プログラムに所属している若手ドライバーたちの去就についても判断を下す役割を担う。 現在レッドブルではギヨーム・ロケリンが若手ドライバープログラムを主導する役割を担っている。ロケリンはセバスチャン・ベッテルが4年連続で世界王者に輝いた時代にレースエンジニアを務め、“ロッキー”の愛称で知られた人物だ。 ラグリュはロケリンと緊密に連携して業務を進めることになる。ロケリンは今後も、ジュニアカテゴリーで戦うレッドブル育成ドライバーたちをサーキットで直接サポートする役割に専念し、ラグリュへ報告を行う立場となるだろう。 この体制は

records.title: Why Fernando Alonso's F1 Future Hinges on the 2026 Regulations, Not Aston Martin's Pace
records.excerpt: Two-time World Champion Fernando Alonso has declared that his Formula 1 future will be decided by the drivability of the 2026 regulation cars, dismissing the immediate impact of Aston Martin's upgrades. Back to News / Sports Sports Why Fernando Alonso's F1 Future Hinges on the 2026 Regulations, Not Aston Martin's Pace Two-time World Champion Fernando Alonso has declared that his Formula 1 future will be decided by the drivability of the 2026 regulation cars, dismissing the immediate impact of Aston Martin's upgrades. SF Streamline Feed Official Verified Jul 21, 2026 Updated Jul 21, 2026 Reading Follow on Google News Fernando Alonso, the relentless two-time Formula 1 World Champion, has fundamentally reframed the narrative surrounding his impending contract expiration. As speculation mounts regarding his tenure with the Silverstone-based Aston Martin squad, the 44-year-old Spaniard has categorically stated that his decision to race beyond 2026 will not be dictated by his team’s immediate aerodynamic performance. Instead, his future entirely hinges on the fundamental drivability and enjoyment extracted from the next generation of Formula 1 hybrid regulations. The revelation introduces a profound philosophical variable into the highly sanitized, data-driven world of modern motorsport. Aston Martin has endured a disastrous opening to the current regulatory cycle, fielding a package plagued by severe weight issues and unpredictable reliability. While team owner Lawrence Stroll desperately banks on a comprehensive B-spec upgrade to salvage the season, Alonso has made it abundantly clear that engineering a marginally faster car is insufficient to retain his services if the core driving experience remains compromised. The Disconnect Between Performance and Passion Speaking with characteristic bluntness at the Spa-Francorchamps circuit, Alonso dismissed the notion that the remainder of the 2026 campaign holds any bearing on his future. He articulated a profound dissatisfaction with the current trajectory of Formula 1 machinery, which has prioritized immense downforce and battery regeneration over the visceral, raw agility that defined earlier eras of the sport. The Weight Penalty: Current F1 cars are the heaviest in the sport's history, exceeding 798 kilograms. This bulk fundamentally blunts cornering agility, transforming tracks like Spa and Silverstone into exercises in momentum management rather than pure mechanical grip. The Hybrid Complexity: Alonso has openly criticized the heavy reliance on complex energy recovery systems, which often dictate driving styles, forcing drivers into rigid delta times and aggressive lift-and-coast fuel management regimes. The Unrealistic Benchmark: “I cannot base my decision for next year on a performance that is not realistic,” Alonso remarked, acknowledging that Aston Martin’s current struggles do not reflect the true operational ceiling of the heavily capitalized factory. Aston Martin’s Desperate High-Stakes Gamble The pressure on Aston Martin is acute. The organization has executed a staggering capital deployment strategy designed specifically to catapult the team into championship contention. The failure to deliver a competitive chassis threatens to destabilize a carefully constructed corporate architecture. The Infrastructure Overhaul: The team recently completed the transition into a state-of-the-art manufacturing facility in the UK’s motorsport valley, complete with a proprietary wind tunnel designed to eliminate reliance on Mercedes' infrastructure. The Technical Leadership: Securing the legendary aerodynamicist Adrian Newey was intended to be the ultimate statement of intent, yet translating his genius into immediate track performance has proven elusive amidst the current rigid cost cap restrictions. The Honda Works Alliance: Aston Martin’s exclusive works engine partnership with Honda, set to commence in line with the new engine regulations, represents a massive operational pivot away from customer status. The 2026 Hybrid Era Dilemma Alonso’s focus is locked firmly on the impending 2026 regulatory overhaul. The FIA is set to introduce a radical redesign of both the power units and the chassis. The new engines will increase the electrical power output to roughly 50 percent of the total 1,000 horsepower, while mandating the use of 100 percent sustainable synthetic fuels. Simultaneously, the governing body is attempting to draft rules for smaller, lighter “nimble cars” featuring active aerodynamics. For Alonso, the calculus is simple: if the 2026 regulations succeed in creating a car that is genuinely thrilling to pilot on the absolute limit, he will extend his unprecedented career. If the cars remain heavy, cumbersome, and entirely dictated by battery deployment algorithms, no amount of financial compensation or aerodynamic upgrades from Aston Martin will prevent his retirement. Global Resonance: From Spa to the Safari Rally Alonso’s critique resonates deeply with motorsport purists across the globe, including East Africa’s massive racing fanbase. In Kenya, where the World Rally Championship (WRC) Safari Rally commands a fanatical following, enthusiasts understand the delicate balance between technological advancement and sheer mechanical spectacle. Just as the WRC recently rolled back plans for expensive hybrid units to preserve the raw appeal of Rally1 cars in the dust of Naivasha, Formula 1 is facing an identical existential crisis on the pristine tarmac of Europe. Whether Fernando Alonso takes to the grid in 2027 will not be decided by a stopwatch in a wind tunnel, but by the fundamental joy of driving a racing car in anger. records.excerpt: Fernando Alonso explains Alonso future decision won’t depend on Aston Martin updates Skip to content Fernando Alonso explains Alonso future decision won’t depend on Aston Martin updates July 20, 2026 by Oliver Valenti Fernando Alonso discusses his future and the factors influencing his decision Fernando Alonso is close to making a decision about his future beyond the 2026 season. Early in the article, Alonso made clear that his Alonso future decision will not depend on the highly anticipated new upgrade package from Aston Martin . This upgrade debuts this weekend at the Hungarian Grand Prix . and on Google News to improve the quality of the articles Performance won’t determine Alonso’s future The Budapest weekend is crucial for the British team’s season as they launch essentially a new version of the AMR26 . Despite the struggles faced so far, Fernando Alonso made it clear the performance of this upgrade will not influence his choice to continue racing in 2027 . “Nothing, because my decision is not tied to this year’s performance. We started off on the wrong foot,” the Spanish driver told RacingNews365 . The Oviedo champion believes the difficulties seen so far do not reflect the team’s true potential. He considers this potential significantly higher than what has been shown on track. Fernando Alonso driving the Aston Martin AMR26 during the Silverstone weekend – Image credit: Marco Talluto for PaddockNews24 The impact of technical regulations The decisive factor for Alonso’s future will be the technical direction that F1 chooses to take. The driver’s concerns mainly focus on the driving enjoyment and feel of the current cars. “Driving these machines at circuits like Silverstone or Spa is not what I dream for my future,” the Asturian openly admitted. The FIA has already confirmed changes for next year’s rules. These changes reduce the strict split between internal combustion engines and batteries in favor of more power from the combustion engine. These regulatory changes will guide the Spanish champion’s final decision during the summer break. As a result, his future in the sport remains uncertain. records.title: F1 launches The Out Lap, a moving restaurant on a flatbed truck
records.excerpt: The Out Lap is a 12-seat fine-dining restaurant on a flatbed truck that laps grand prix circuits, launched by F1 with LVMH's Moet Hennessy at Spa. Twelve seats, one truck, and a very long waiting list Formula 1 has never struggled to invent new tiers of exclusivity , but this one is unusually literal. The Out Lap is a fine-dining restaurant built into a container, mounted on the back of a flatbed truck, and driven around a grand prix circuit while twelve guests eat dinner. It debuted at Spa-Francorchamps, which for a Belgian audience makes it rather more than a curiosity. How it actually works The truck follows a route tailored to each grand prix, serving courses as it moves and stopping at the circuit's landmark corners so guests can step out and take in the place properly. The package also includes guided access to the main paddock and a private visit to the Cool Down Room, the space where drivers decompress immediately after a race and where almost nobody outside the sport ever sets foot. The food and the sponsor The partner is Moet Hennessy, the wines and spirits arm of LVMH, and the pairings come from its portfolio. Menus are curated locally by renowned chefs at each venue rather than shipped in wholesale, so the Spa edition is meant to taste different from whatever follows at the next European round. It is a sensible piece of design: the one thing a travelling restaurant can genuinely offer is a different place each time. The storytellers Mika Hakkinen and Jacques Villeneuve are on board as ambassadors, and their role is the part that actually sounds worth the money. Both recount pivotal moments from their careers at the exact corners where those moments happened, which at Spa gives them a great deal of material to work with. What it costs, sort of Nobody is publishing a price. The Out Lap is positioned as an add-on for Paddock Club pass holders, and a three-day Paddock Club pass already runs comfortably into five figures before anyone opens a bottle. Twelve seats per session at each race is about as narrow as hospitality gets, so the number is likely to stay quiet. Where it runs For this season The Out Lap is limited to European rounds, having launched at Spa. F1 has not confirmed whether it travels further afield in 2027, though a concept this portable is unlikely to stay on one continent for long. AutoNext Take It would be easy to file this under yet another way for Formula 1 to charge the wealthy more money, and that criticism is not wrong. But strip away the champagne and the idea underneath is genuinely good: stopping at Eau Rouge with a former world champion explaining what happened there is the kind of access no grandstand ticket buys , and circuits are far more interesting from inside them than from a seat above. The practical question nobody seems to have asked is whether a tasting menu survives Spa's elevation changes. Anyone who has been driven up through Raidillon knows the sensation, and it is not obviously compatible with a full glass. Perhaps that is what the stops are really for. War In Iran Could Force Formula 1 To Cancel Two More Races by AutoGuide.com News Staff (IC: employee) Published: July 22nd, 2026 Share Image: Formula 1 The 2026 Formula 1 World Championship calendar remains subject to adjustment as the sport navigates the ongoing operational and logistical fallout from the American-Iranian conflict. Regional instability has already left a major dent in the early-season schedule, and decision deadlines are rapidly approaching regarding whether the year-end itinerary will be safely completed or fundamentally restructured. The disruptions initially forced the total cancellation of both the Bahrain and Saudi Arabian Grands Prix. These decisions were made just as sea freight was preparing to depart Europe, resulting in an unplanned five-week spring hiatus for the paddock. While those cancellations temporarily trimmed the ambitious 24-race schedule down to 22 events, behind-the-scenes negotiations indicate the sport has not entirely given up on its original multi-race footprint. The Push for a Summer Calendar Expansion Formula 1 CEO Stefano Domenicali has confirmed that the window to restore one of the dropped spring events back to the calendar is closing fast. Paddock executives are aiming to use a looming mid-season deadline to salvage a 23-race itinerary. Speaking on the matter, Domenicali indicated that any viable opening to execute a previously canceled event must be definitively finalized prior to the upcoming August summer shutdown. The current proposal targets placing the Bahrain Grand Prix at the permanent Sakhir circuit onto a vacant autumn date nestled directly between the Azerbaijan and Singapore rounds. While Saudi Arabia has largely avoided direct engagement in the fighting, Bahrain remains a logistically complicated military variable in the wider territory. Should the reinstatement clear all security hurdles, it would present a massive vote of structural confidence. However, it would also require teams to absorb a grueling marathon of nine races packed into a mere 11-week window, characterized by three consecutive triple-header events. Image: Red Bull Content Pool High Stakes for Year-End Middle Eastern Flyaways While an expansion option sits on the table for the summer break, a second, more critical deadline looms in the autumn regarding the final two legs of the championship. Deep safety concerns linger over moving equipment, teams, and personnel through the volatile Strait of Hormuz to reach the planned season-ending venues. F1 leadership has designated mid-September as the final operational cutoff date to evaluate the stability of the Gulf region. Under the primary calendar layout, the Qatar Grand Prix is scheduled for November 29 at the Lusail International Circuit, with the season finale at Abu Dhabi locked in for the subsequent weekend on December 6. Image: Scuderia Ferrari HP The Portuguese Backup Contingency Acknowledging that geopolitical escalations could block safe passage to the final venues, Formula 1 management has established a fully functional fallback security net. If the mid-September assessment reveals that shipping lanes and venues are compromised, the sport is prepared to drop the final Middle Eastern rounds entirely and trigger its backup plan. Under this secondary scenario, the Autódromo Internacional do Algarve in Portimão, Portugal, stands ready to assume hosting duties. Portimão would step in to anchor a substitute European season finale immediately following the high-profile street race at the Las Vegas Grand Prix. Triggering this alternative framework would automatically truncate the championship down to a 21-race calendar—the shortest season itinerary executed by the sport since the pandemic-disrupted 2020 campaign. Domenicali stressed that maintaining these proactive logistical contingencies is a fundamental duty of a professional sporting promoter, confirming that a comprehensive operational roadmap is firmly in place regardless of how the geopolitical environment develops over the coming months. records.excerpt: Marvel Announces "Iron Man: Racing Towards Doom" Formula 1 Comic with Williams Racing Subscribe Fun & Games | Wait Times | Top 24 Stories Subscribe What We're Covering San Diego Comic-Con 2026 Disney Worldbuilders Teaser Avengers: Doomsday Trailer Disney NFL Champion Collection D23 Schedule - Sortable and Searchable SDCC 2026 Schedules LP On Balance Podcast Ep. 35 LP On Location - Descendants: Wicked Wonderland Premiere Fun & Games Sorcerer's Streak Villain's Challenge Disney Hangman Disney Quizzes Disney Park Maps Through the Years Iron Man Joins Williams Racing Drivers in New Formula 1-Inspired Marvel Comic Carlos Sainz and Alex Albon join Iron Man, Black Widow, Captain America, and more in a high-speed adventure against Doctor Doom. by Luke Manning | Jul 22, 2026 10:55am (Pacific) Tags: Marvel , Marvel Comics , Iron Man , Formula 1 , Doctor Doom Marvel Comics and Williams Racing are teaming up for Iron Man: Racing Towards Doom #1 , a new one-shot arriving this October. What's Happening: Combining the thrills of Formula 1 racing with Marvel super hero storytelling, the issue is written by Ethan Sacks with artwork by Greg Land. Iron Man joins Atlassian Williams F1 Team drivers Carlos Sainz and Alex Albon to stop Doctor Doom, who is determined to ensure Latveria comes out on top. The adventure will also feature appearances by Black Widow, Captain America, and other Marvel heroes. The story follows Sainz and Albon as they face a Latverian threat both on and off the track before a final showdown with Doctor Doom. " When high-speed tech collides with world-shaking danger, Iron Man must take the lead! Atlassian Williams F1 Team star drivers Carlos Sainz and Alex Albon face a Latverian threat on and off the track. But at the finish line, Doctor Doom waits, and he’s playing for keeps!!!" Writer Ethan Sacks said the comic is designed to introduce Williams Racing fans to Marvel comics while also giving Marvel fans a taste of the excitement of Formula 1. Sacks also praised Greg Land's racing sequences and the collaboration with Williams Racing, calling the team-up between Iron Man, the Avengers, Sainz, Albon, and Doctor Doom "a Marvel Team-Up for the ages." Check out Phil Noto’s cover and preorder Iron Man: Racing Towards Doom #1 at your local comic shop today. More Marvel News: Avengers: Doomsday pulled in an incredible $16.5 million in first-day advance ticket sales , with premium screenings already selling out ahead of its December 18 release. Deadpool will return ...eventually. At least according to Deadpool himself, Ryan Reynolds. With just over a week to go until the release of Spider-Man: Brand New Day , the final trailer for the highly-anticipated film has arrived. The official trailer for Avengers: Doomsday is here, and it shows off the massive cast of the upcoming film. Plus, dive deeper into the questions we have about the film following the trailer's release.

records.title: その剣幕をドイツだけは見ていた…F1公式が伏せたラッセル無線、ベルギー事故直後の怒声が後に判明
records.excerpt: copyright FORMULA 1 その剣幕をドイツだけは見ていた…F1公式が伏せたラッセル無線、ベルギー事故直後の怒声が後に判明 Published： 2026/7/21 12:28 2026年F1第10戦ベルギーGPのオープニングラップでリタイヤを強いられたジョージ・ラッセル（メルセデス）が、事故直後のチーム無線で激しい剣幕を見せ、苛立ちを爆発させていたことが分かった。 この無線通信は、F1の公式国際放送やオンボード映像では無音処理されており、多くの視聴者は目にすることができなかった。だが、SNSやドイツメディアを通じて後に発覚する事態となった。 判明したラッセルの怒声「こんなの受け入れられない！」 レ・コーム（ターン5）でルイス・ハミルトン（フェラーリ）と接触してグラベルに捕らわれた際、ラッセルが手ぶりを交えて何かを叫ぶ様子が見られた。 だが、国際放送やオンボード映像、さらにはF1公式SNSで公開された以下の動画にも音声は含まれていなかった。 View this post on Instagram その後、SNSやドイツメディアを通じて、怒りの発言内容が明らかになった。ラッセルはケメル・ストレートで、 全てのメルセデス製パワーユニット（PU）が抱えた問題 によるバッテリー残量不足に見舞われ、無防備な状態に陥って後続にのみ込まれたことに激怒していた。 「終わった！ SoC（充電状態）は一体どうなってんだ！？ ストレートでバッテリーが全くなかった！……みんな、こんなの受け入れられない！ 今週末ずっとそうだ！ マジであり得ない！」とラッセルは、放送禁止用語を交えながらチームに対して、文字通りの怒鳴り声を上げていた。 この無線内容についてイギリスの専門メディア『The Race』は、国際中継やオンボード映像では検閲によりカットされたものの、公式配信サービス『F1 TV』のドイツ語版だけは、この無線を独自に取り上げて配信したと伝えている。 激昂無線を伏せたF1公式、その理由と是非 国際放送でこの発言が流れなかった明確な理由は不明だが、同メディアは「ラッセルが使用した不適切な言葉遣いが理由だった」としている。いずれにせよ、偶発的ではなく意図的に伏せられたのは明白だろう。 この事故により、ラッセルはノーポイントに終わり、ドライバーズ・ランキング3位に後退した。タイトル争いで大きな痛手を受けただけに、事故直後に何を語るのかは大きな関心を集めるものだった。 それでも、F1公式はその発言を徹底して取り上げなかった。 各週末後に公開される恒例の「 Radio Rewind 」でも、接触相手であるハミルトンの無線を取り上げた一方、ラッセルの無線は先程の冒頭の一言に限られた。17分10秒に及ぶこの動画で、ラッセルの発言として収録されたのは「終わった！」のみで、以降は全てカットされている。 レース中には、22人のドライバーと各チームのエンジニアとの間で絶え間なくやり取りが続けられている。その中から、フォーミュラ・ワン・マネジメント（FOM）のテレビディレクターは国際映像で流す内容を取捨選択している。 罵り言葉や、攻撃的な表現は放送されないか、あるいは場合によっては電子音、いわゆる「ピー音」で伏されて放送される。こうした検閲は無論、F1のイメージ保護という目的もあるだろう。だがFOMは、ドライバーやチームへの誹謗中傷を防ぐことを検閲の理由として挙げている。 国際映像は幅広い文化的背景を持つ視聴者に届くため、担当ディレクターに慎重な配慮が求められることは確かだろう。 一方で今回の件は、物議を醸す新たなレギュレーションがもたらした負の側面と言える部分もあるだけに、少なくともその事実が判明した後の「Radio Rewind」に関しては、取り上げることで視聴者に考える材料を提供する意義はあったという見方も可能だろう。 F1ベルギーGP特集 TAG： おすすめ F1 ラッセル メルセデス F1ベルギーGP googlePreferred Google優先ソースに追加 records.title: メルセデス・ベンツ、EV専用プラットフォーム採用の「Electric GLC」が事前契約11日で1,000件突破
records.excerpt: メルセデス・ベンツコリアの初の純電気SUV「The all-new Mercedes-Benz Electric GLC」の事前契約が、受付開始から11日間で1,000件を突破した。同車はメルセデス・ベンツのEV専用アーキテクチャ「MB.EA」を初採用し、AIベースの次世代OS「MB.OS」を搭載。WLTPモードで最大航続距離616km、800V急速充電システムを備え、価格は9,000万ウォン（約990万円）から。顧客への納車は2026年第4四半期を予定している。一方、同時期に事前契約を開始した「The new S-Class」と「The new Maybach S-Class」も2,200台を記録し、高金利環境下におけるプレミアム車への旺盛な需要を示した。 メルセデス・ベンツコリアは20日、中型SUV「GLC」初の純電気モデル「The all-new Mercedes-Benz Electric GLC」の事前契約が11日間で1,000件を突破したと発表した。同社は今月9日から韓国全国65カ所の正規販売店と公式ウェブサイトを通じて事前契約を受け付けており、20日時点で契約台数が1,000台を超えたという。 今回の事前契約の成果は、韓国消費者のプレミアムEVに対する高い関心を反映している。これに先立ち、メルセデス・ベンツコリアはフラッグシップセダン「The new S-Class」と「The new Maybach S-Class」の事前契約でも、わずか3日間で2,200台を記録しており、下半期の輸入車市場におけるプレミアム・電動化攻勢を強めている。 The all-new Electric GLCは、メルセデス・ベンツのEV専用アーキテクチャ「MB.EA」を初めて採用したモデルだ。従来のGLCが持つSUVとしてのアイデンティティに、電気駆動システムと人工知能（AI）ベースの次世代オペレーティングシステム「MB.OS」を組み合わせ、走行性能とソフトウェア体験を同時に引き上げたことが特徴である。車両にはブランドを象徴する新しいアイコニック・イルミネーテッド・ラジエーターグリルが採用され、インフォテインメントシステム「MBUXバーチャルアシスタント」は、ChatGPTやMicrosoft BingなどのAIおよび検索技術を活用し、改善された音声支援サービスを提供する。 韓国市場にはまず、「GLC 300 4MATIC AMG Line Electric」と「GLC 300 4MATIC AMG Line+ Electric」のローンチエディション2モデルが導入され、顧客への納車は2026年第4四半期から開始される予定だ。価格は付加価値税と個別消費税5％を反映した基準で、それぞれ9,000万ウォン（約990万円）、9,480万ウォン（約1,000万円）となる。上位グレードの「GLC 400 4MATIC Electric」は2027年上半期の発売を予定しており、価格は発売時点で公開される。 性能面では、GLC 300 4MATIC Electricは最高出力310kWを発揮し、欧州基準（WLTP）で最大航続距離616kmを確保した。800V急速充電システムを導入し、韓国国内の330kW級DC急速充電器を使用した場合、バッテリー容量10％から80％まで約22分で充電できる。 メルセデス・ベンツコリアはElectric GLCに加え、フラッグシップラインアップの事前契約も同時に進め、下半期の輸入車市場を攻略している。5月18日から20日まで受け付けられたThe new S-ClassとThe new Maybach S-Classの事前契約台数は2,200台に達した。The new S-Classは、車両を構成する部品の50％以上にあたる2,700点の要素が新たに開発または再設計され、一世代の中で行われ得る最も広範なアップデートとの評価を受けている。同モデル史上初めてイルミネーテッドグリルが採用され、新しいデジタルライト・ツインスター・ヘッドランプデザインによってフラッグシップセダンとしての存在感を強調した。 The new S-Classは全6モデルで構成され、価格は1億5,400万ウォン（約1,700万円）から2億7,000万ウォン（約2,980万円）まで。The new Maybach S-Classは3モデルで発売され、3億1,700万ウォン（約3,490万円）から4億700万ウォン（約4,480万円）の価格帯となる。メルセデス・ベンツコリアはS-Classの発売を記念し、各140台限定販売のローンチエディション「AMG Line Plus Edition」と「Sparkling Black Edition」も同時に発表した。 このようにメルセデス・ベンツコリアが、EV専用プラットフォームを搭載した中型SUVから超高額フラッグシップセダンに至るまで新車ラインアップを一斉に投入したことで、高金利と消費低迷の中でも1億ウォン（約1,100万円）超の高額モデルやプレミアムEVに需要が集中する現象が、下半期の輸入車市場の競争構図をさらに激化させる見通しだ。

records.excerpt: Aston Martin raises £550M from HPS Investment Partners Español Sections Bitcoin DeFi Ethereum NFTs AI Agents Regulation Web3 Business Ecosystem Sections Soccer Esports Aston Martin raises £550M from HPS Investment Partners Luxury automaker secures hefty financing amid cash challenges and market hurdles Share Add us on Google by Editorial Team Jul. 22, 2026 Luxury carmaker Aston Martin has secured a significant cash infusion of £550 million from HPS Investment Partners, a step aimed at strengthening its financial footing. The move comes as the company faces substantial cash-burn issues and a steep decline in its share value, which has plummeted by roughly 44% this year. A fresh injection of liquidity The funding package primarily consists of a £450 million senior secured term loan, complemented by a £100 million delayed draw term loan. Additionally, there is an extra £100 million reserved in permitted debt capacity. Combined, these measures elevate Aston Martin’s liquidity levels to approximately £340 million as of June 30, 2026. Not exactly chump change, but certainly a necessity considering the company’s current financial landscape. This financial lifeline from HPS — owned by BlackRock, one of the largest asset management companies globally — is timely. Aston Martin’s issues aren’t confined to dwindling stock prices. The luxury automaker grapples with weak demand from China and tariffs from the US that have hit its sales hard. Timing, as they say, is everything, and for Aston Martin, this is about playing financial catch-up in a challenging environment. Advertisement Navigating luxury amid market storms Turning the headlights to market implications, this financing provides Aston Martin with a crucial cushion as it maneuvers through economic turbulence. The challenge is twofold: stabilizing its current operations while looking at strategies to rejuvenate sales. The cash injection suggests a proactive attempt to do just that — offering a lifeline to shore up investor confidence and market perception. The luxury vehicle market is like an exclusive club. If you’re not in, you’re really not in. Aston Martin’s move to secure such a large financing package shows it’s serious about remaining a key player in the high-stakes luxury car industry. And with financial backers like HPS, they’re likely to get a second chance to steer into profitable territory. Crypto crossover and emerging trends So, what does all this mean for the crypto-savvy investor? Direct links to the cryptocurrency market are not evident in this transaction. However, it’s worth noting that Aston Martin has previously shown interest in embracing digital assets, hinting at future potential in integrating digital currency options for purchasing their high-end vehicles. Imagine driving away a brand new Aston with a wallet full of Bitcoin — quite the possibility in our digital future. In the bigger picture, the luxury automaker seems open to tapping into emerging markets like digital currencies, which could become a lucrative domain in the coming years. For now, the company remains focused on stabilizing its core business, but the possibility of a digital pivot could attract a tech-forward clientele. For investors keeping an eye on how traditional industries could blend with modern technology, Aston Martin’s moves could be a signal of things to come. Whether they shift into that gear remains to be seen, but the path appears laid out. Disclosure: This article was edited by Editorial Team. records.title: Speciale "FIA 2026". GKN Aerospace amplia la partnership con Pratt & Whitney tra motori civili e programma F-35
records.excerpt: GKN Aerospace rafforza la collaborazione con Pratt & Whitney attraverso un duplice accordo che interessa sia il settore dell’aviazione commerciale sia quello della difesa. Annunciata in occasione del "Farnborough International Airshow"-FIA- (20-24 luglio), l’intesa amplia la partnership industriale tra... Speciale "FIA 2026". GKN Aerospace amplia la partnership con Pratt & Whitney tra motori civili e programma F-35 Nuovi accordi per la produzione dei componenti dei motori GTF e lo sviluppo della manifattura additiva GKN Aerospace rafforza la collaborazione con Pratt & Whitney attraverso un duplice accordo che interessa sia il settore dell’aviazione commerciale sia quello della difesa. Annunciata in occasione del "Farnborough International Airshow"-FIA- (20-24 luglio), l’intesa amplia la partnership industriale tra le due aziende con nuove attività produttive sui motori della famiglia Geared Turbofan (GTF) e con un programma di sviluppo dedicato alla manifattura additiva del propulsore F135, che equipaggia il caccia Lockheed Martin F-35. Il primo accordo prevede l’estensione della collaborazione nella produzione delle palette statoriche del compressore di bassa pressione destinate ai motori PW1500G e PW1900G, impiegati rispettivamente sugli Airbus A-220 e sugli Embraer E-JetE2. L’intesa comprende inoltre il supporto per l’intero ciclo di vita dei componenti, consolidando il ruolo di GKN Aerospace all’interno della catena di fornitura di Pratt & Whitney. L’ampliamento delle attività garantirà continuità produttiva allo stabilimento GKN di Newington, nel Connecticut, dove l’azienda realizza questi componenti dal 2018. L’incremento delle lavorazioni consentirà di sostenere la produzione dei motori destinati a due dei principali programmi dell’aviazione regionale ed a corridoio singolo di nuova generazione. Parallelamente, le due società hanno avviato un nuovo programma tecnologico dedicato all’impiego della manifattura additiva per la realizzazione di grandi componenti strutturali del motore F135. Il progetto punta a sfruttare il processo proprietario di deposizione laser di metallo con filo sviluppato da GKN Aerospace, con l’obiettivo di produrre componenti a grande scala compatibili con il propulsore che equipaggia il caccia di quinta generazione. Le attività saranno condotte principalmente presso il sito di Kongsberg, in Norvegia, con il supporto della Norwegian Defence Materiel Agency, a conferma dell’interesse dei Paesi partner del programma F-35 nello sviluppo di tecnologie produttive più efficienti. L’iniziativa si inserisce nel più ampio processo di innovazione della filiera aerospaziale, dove la produzione additiva sta assumendo un ruolo sempre più strategico per ridurre tempi di realizzazione, costi e impatto dei processi industriali. dab - 1270024 Farnborough, Regno Unito, 21/07/2026 07:50 AVIONEWS - World Aeronautical Press Agency Simili Compagnie Turkish Airlines aderisce al fondo Saffa Per accelerare produzione Saf Turkish Airlines ha sottoscritto un accordo per partecipare a Saffa Fund (Sustainable Aviation Fuel Financing Alliance) un fondo di investimento gestito da Burnham Sterling Asset Management LLC (Bsam)... continua Aviazione civile Farnborough. Secure .gov websites use HTTPS A lock ( ) or https:// means you’ve safely connected to the .gov website. Share sensitive information only on official, secure websites. United States Department of Transportation Commercial Space Transportation Countdown to launch. The FAA has reached a historic milestone with successful launch and reentry operations. See Stats Here FAA Reaches 1,000 Licensed Space Operations August 14, 2025 marked the FAA’s 1,000th operation of a commercial space vehicle that the agency licensed or permitted. The United States is a leader in space exploration, and this milestone highlights more than 35 years of the FAA successfully fulfilling its mission to protect safety and advance the future of our skies. The commercial space transportation industry emerged in the 1990s and was primarily used to launch commercial satellites and transport cargo to the International Space Station (ISS). In just the last few years, growing interest in commercial space is realizing new possibilities for the industry including providing transportation to the ISS laboratories for research and space tourism. This rapidly growing industry is inspiring scientists, engineers, teachers, and a whole generation, to imagine entirely new possibilities for the future of space. Safety Safety is our North Star. Compliance, Enforcement & Mishap Legislation & Policies Operations We protect the public, property, and U.S. national security interests. Airspace Integration Commercial Space Data Licensing We license all U.S. commercial launches and reentries here and abroad. Environmental Licenses, Permits and Approvals Stakeholder Engagement Vehicle Operator Licenses Industry Outreach We work collaboratively with industry to promote safety. Aerospace Rulemaking Committees: (SpARCs) COMSTAC Standards Development International We work with our international partners to promote safety. International Affairs Spaceports U.S. Spaceports are critical infrastructure for the industry. Office of Spaceports Spaceports by State Commercial Space By The Numbers Spaceports Map Find a U.S. spaceport near you. Map to commercial, government, and active private spaceports around the country. Learn about U.S. Spaceports Jobs What do we do? What careers are in commercial space? Commercial Space Transportation ensures that rocket launches and reentries are safe. We do this by applying a broad range of skillsets to manage licensing and regulatory work, as well as many programs and initiatives. Some examples of the jobs we do include inspecting reusable and expendable launch vehicles, assessing aerospace vehicle systems, developing public safety standards and requirements, assuring engineering quality, and assessing environmental impacts. Why does it matter? Our efforts help facilitate both the U.S. and global commercial space transportation industry’s health and growth. We value the talents, ideas, and insights that will enable us to continue our mission of ensuring and promoting the safest commercial space transportation in the world. Join us in exploring this exciting, meaningful, and innovative field! How can I find out more and apply? We are actively hiring qualified people to help us grow our team to meet the global commercial space community’s increasing demands. If you would like to find out more about being part of an organization where the possibilities are literally limitless, please take a look at Commercial Space Careers and email us at 9-AST-Comm-Space-Careers@faa.gov . records.title: Tesla Investors Want Answers About a Potential Merger With SpaceX
records.excerpt: Tesla investors are responding to rampant speculation about a mega-merger with SpaceX, which raised $86 billion in a blockbuster IPO last month. Whispers that Elon Musk might combine Tesla and SpaceX are growing — and investors want answers. Shareholders took to an online Tesla investor forum to submit questions for executives ahead of the company's second-quarter earnings and clamor for more details about a rumored merger with SpaceX. "Will SpaceX merge with Tesla?" asked one retail investor, in a question representing around 100,000 Tesla shares. Others asked if investors would get a vote on any proposed merger and how executives would ensure that a tie-up treats Tesla investors fairly. One retail investor asked how Musk would balance his compensation plan, which requires the Tesla CEO to hit a series of ambitious goals to unlock the full $1 trillion payout, with a SpaceX merger. "To reward long-term Tesla retail shareholders for their loyalty, can you commit to achieving at least half of the goals outlined in your 2025 compensation plan before considering any offers to acquire or merge Tesla?" they wrote in a post that has received nearly 300 votes. Musk's goals include passing 20 million EV sales, 10 million Full Self-Driving subscriptions, and deploying 1 million robotaxis and Optimus robots. While the majority of questions on the Q&A platform were focused on Tesla's sluggish robotaxi rollout and plans for Optimus, Business Insider counted at least 20 questions about the potential merger, making it one of the most-discussed topics among investors. It's a sign that Tesla investors are increasingly responding to rampant speculation about a mega-merger with SpaceX, which raised a record $86 billion in a blockbuster IPO last month. Longtime Tesla investor Ross Gerber told Business Insider he expected the merger to come up in Tesla's Q2 earnings call on Wednesday. "I expect management to downplay it, because on the surface it does not create obvious value for either company. It would be complicated, distracting, and difficult to structure in a way that makes everyone happy," said Gerber, who is the CEO of wealth management firm Gerber Kawasaki. Gerber added that the slow pace of Tesla's robotaxi expansion, which he said underpinned the company's $1.4 trillion valuation, is investors' main focus right now. However, he still expects a tie-up with SpaceX to happen eventually. "SpaceX is where much of the innovation and excitement is right now, while Tesla's core EV business is under increasing pressure," Gerber said. "If investor interest continues shifting away from EVs and toward SpaceX's growth story, a merger may become a way to reframe Tesla around Elon's stronger innovation platform," he added. Tesla and SpaceX's share prices have both languished in the past month. Tesla's stock is down nearly 8%, while SpaceX has fallen 35% as the rocket maker's shares tumbled from their post-IPO peak. Investors and Tesla bulls previously told Business Insider that a combination would make it easier for the two companies, which are already heavily intertwined, to work together. SpaceX and Tesla are already collaborating on Musk's Terafab chip-building moonshot, and SpaceX president Gwynne Shotwell didn't rule out a merger last month. "That might make Elon's life a little easier, actually," Shotwell said. "There's no question that there's synergies between Tesla and SpaceX in our futures, definitely, there's a convergence of a kind of what we're all trying to accomplish in the future," she added.

(SpaceX) SpaceX to launch Starship 13 in second test flight attempt BY Anthony Leone and Jon Shaban Texas UPDATED 6:41 PM ET Jul. 22, 2026 PUBLISHED 1:23 PM ET Jul. 22, 2026 PUBLISHED 1:23 PM EDT Jul. 22, 2026 SHARE BOCA CHICA BEACH, Texas — SpaceX will attempt for a second time to launch the Starship 13 flight on Thursday evening after engine issues caused an abort during the first try last week. What You Need To Know Two Raptor 3 engines have been replaced on the Super Heavy rocket booster Chopsticks will not catch Super Heavy rocket booster for 13th test Starship is the spacecraft, and the Super Heavy is the rocket booster When they are stacked together, they are called Starship SpaceX made corrections to the issues discovered in the last mission Get more space coverage here ▶ 🔻Scroll down to learn about the Starship's test flights🔻 SpaceX stated that the uncrewed Starship is all set to take off from the company’s Starbase facility in Boca Chica, Texas, for its suborbital test flight. The 90-minute launch window is set to open at 6:45 p.m. ET for the 407-foot (124 meters) tall rocket that NASA hopes will be used to land humans back on the moon during the Artemis IV mission in 2028. SpaceX stated that weather is a concern for the launch due to Tropical Storm Bertha . This new-generation Starship is 10 feet (3 meters) taller than the previous versions that were tested before flight 12. The first launch attempt During the first launch attempt of the Starship 13 flight test on Thursday, July 16, the countdown clock reached zero and flames and smoke were seen, but the massive rocket did not leave the launch pad. Minutes after the launch attempt, SpaceX founder Elon Musk explained on X that some of the 33 Raptor 3 engines did not fire, thus triggering an automatic launch abort for the mission. He said that two of the Raptor 3 engines have been replaced on the Super Heavy booster rocket. During the live feed of the launch, SpaceX Communications manager Daniel Huot said a hold was triggered from the booster. The triggered hold scrubbed any further attempts at liftoff for that Thursday night, he stated. &amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;nbsp; What to expected from the 13th test flight Starship is the spacecraft, and Super Heavy is the rocket booster. When assembled, they are jointly called Starship. Scroll down to see the Starship flight tests timeline and the issues witnessed in the last test. SpaceX shared information about what will be expected for the flight. The Starship, which will be part of NASA’s Artemis III mission next year, will demonstrate a number of important tasks. The Super Heavy booster will be taken through its paces. “The booster’s primary test objective will be executing a successful launch, ascent, stage separation, boostback burn, and landing burn at an offshore landing point in the Gulf of America,” the company stated . Which means it will not be caught by the launch tower’s metal arms, known as the chopsticks. Hours before the first flight attempt, Dr. Don Platt, director of Florida Tech's Spaceport Education, shared with Spectrum News some of the things people can look for during the Starship test launch. "Well, one of the first things that you should look at is, even during the launch itself and when the booster is still fairly low, you can see all of those lit engines on the bottom of the rocket. And just look to see that all of them are lit. For a few of these missions, we've seen one or two that are dark," he said. "And so that means those rocket engines are not operational." View this post on Instagram A post shared by Spectrum News 13 (@news13) Platt said Starship is the biggest rocket ever developed and called it a complex vehicle. "Two stages that are very different from one another. New rocket propellant systems that have really not been used that often before. So there's a huge amount of development that has gone into getting us to this point. You know, there certainly have been a few hiccups here and there, but basically their philosophy is to build it and then test it," he said. During the 12th test, the Super Heavy booster experienced issues and could not re-light some of the Raptor 3 engines after stage separation. For the 13th test launch, the newest booster had hardware modifications to improve the re-light system, stated SpaceX. The company did not state how many of the Raptor 3 engines will be used for its flip and water landing in the Gulf; the booster has a total of 33 Raptor engines. Platt also shared what people should be on the look out for during the launch. View this post on Instagram A post shared by Spectrum News 13 (@news13) Starship’s upper stage, which one day astronauts may use to go to the moon in the Artemis IV mission, will have its own set of goals to accomplish. “The Starship upper stage’s primary objectives include the deployment of 20 Starlink V3 satellites, a relight of a single Raptor engine while in space, and another controlled entry, descent, and splashdown in the Indian Ocean. There have also been several modifications to Starship’s propulsion system to address the engine out issue experienced on the previous flight,” the Texas-based company revealed. And these are actual V3 Starlink satellites, not the simulators that were seen in previous tests. These 20 Starlink satellites have their own tasks to perform. They will extend their solar arrays and antennas and attempt to connect to the Starlink constellation, which has more than 9,000 satellites in operational orbit. The 20 Starlink satellites will be in the same suborbital orbit as Starship, and six of them are modified with cameras to scan the craft’s heat shield and send photos back down to mission control. However, all of them will eventually burn up on re-entry 20 minutes after deployment. records.excerpt: SpaceX launches novel geosynchronous robotic servicing satellite on decade-long mission – Spaceflight Now July 23, 2026 Breaking News [ July 21, 2026 ] SpaceX launches novel geosynchronous robotic servicing satellite on decade-long mission Falcon 9 [ July 16, 2026 ] Post-ignition anomaly causes abort of SpaceX’s Starship Flight 13 Artemis [ July 4, 2026 ] Semiconductor manufacturing test bed flies alongside Starlink satellites on Falcon 9 launch Falcon 9 [ July 1, 2026 ] SpaceX launches 24 Starlink satellites on Falcon 9 rocket from Vandenberg SFB Falcon 9 [ June 30, 2026 ] Astronauts ‘operate’ on space station’s broken robot arm Mission Reports SpaceX launches novel geosynchronous robotic servicing satellite on decade-long mission July 21, 2026 Will Robinson-Smith A SpaceX Falcon 9 rocket lifts off from Space Launch Complex 40 at Cape Canaveral Space Force Station on July 21, 2026. Onboard was the U.S. Naval Research Laboratory’s Robotic Servicing of Geosynchronous Satellites (RSGS), the main payload on Northrop Grumman’s Mission Robotic Vehicle spacecraft. There were also three Mission Extension Pods from Northrop Grumman onboard. Image: John Pisani/Spaceflight Now A SpaceX Falcon 9 rocket launched from Cape Canaveral Tuesday carrying Northrop Grumman’s Mission Robotic Vehicle (MRV) and three Mission Extension Pods (MEPs), a novel mission designed to prolog the lifespans of multiple satellites. The MRV is equipped with the Robotic Servicing of Geosynchronous Satellites (RSGS) payload, a pair of robotic arms with an array of tool attachments developed at the U.S. Naval Research Laboratory with financial backing from the Defense Advanced Research Projects Agency (DARPA). Following its launch in summer 2026, Northrop Grumman’s Mission Robotic Vehicle (left) will install Mission Extension Pod (right) jetpacks to extend the lives of client satellites in geosynchronous orbit. MRV also can perform inspection, relocation, repairs, upgrades, and other missions yet to be imagined. Illustration credit: Northrop Grumman Following deployment, the MRV and MEPs will spend a year heading out to geosynchronous Earth orbit. Once there, the MRV will begin the process of installing MEPs onto clients’ spacecraft, including those owned by Australia-based company Optus and Luxembourg-based company SES. The MEPs, which carry fresh supplies of maneuvering fuel, are designed to provide up to eight years of additional life for a satellite. Liftoff from Space Launch Complex 40 occurred at 5:15 p.m. EDT (2115 UTC). The rocket flew due east upon leaving the launch pad. ﻿ SpaceX launched the mission using the Falcon 9 first stage booster B1069, which made its 32nd and final flight. The company said this would be the boosters final mission “Due to the additional performance needed to launch these payloads to geosynchronous transfer orbit.” In addition to 27 batches of Starlink satellites, B1069 launched the following missions: Dec. 21, 2021 – NASA’s CRS-24 Oct. 15, 2022 – Eutelsat’s Hotbird 13F Dec. 8, 2022 – OneWeb’s OneWeb Mission 15 Mar. 17, 2023 – SES’ SES-18 & 19 Decades in the making The concept behind the RSGS goes back more than 20 years when the NRL began examining the possibility of two uncrewed spacecraft performing autonomous rendezvous and docking operations. In the early 2000s, that evolved into a study called ‘RescueSat’, looking at how to recover a satellite stuck in the wrong orbit, and eventually the Spacecraft for the Universal Modification of Orbits (SUMO) program. “The SUMO mandate was daunting. DARPA challenged us to design a robot that could dock with any satellite in space,” said Glen Henshaw, Ph.D., NRL Lead Space Roboticist for RSGS in a prelaunch statement. “We then realized a universal truth—every satellite got to space on a rocket! By targeting the sturdy ‘launch vehicle interface plane’—the structural ring or explosive bolt holes that attach a spacecraft to a rocket for launch—we determined that a robotic arm could safely grapple almost any spacecraft without damaging delicate instruments.” The MRV inside Northrop Grumman’s Dulles, Va., Satellite Manufacturing Facility. Image: Northrop Grumman After proving the concept was possible, by 2005 the SUMO program shifted to the Front End Robotics Enabling Near-term Demonstration (FREND). That program would go onto develop spaceflight worthy robotic arms through a commercial vendor. Alliance Spacesystems, Inc. (ASI), the company who built the robotic arms for NASA’s Mars Curiosity Rover, was selected and environmental testing began in 2008. To find a good business case for these arms, a series of studies were conducted, including a joint NASA-DARPA study in 2012 called the Manned GEO Servicing study. Ultimately, DARPA moved the technology back into what the NRL called “research and hardware maturation via a spaceflight concept program called Phoenix.” After years of studying and contemplation, DARPA decided to proceed with what was then called the RSGS payload to pursue “ultra-close inspection, orbital ‘tow truck’ relocation, mechanical anomaly repair, and upgrading satellites not originally designed to be upgraded.” Four years later in 2019, it selected SpaceLogistics, a Northrop Grumman company to combine the RSGS with the MRV. Following initial checkouts, the RSGS program will be turned over to the U.S. Space Force in support of its Servicing, Mobility, and Logistics portfolio. A Northrop Grumman employee at the company’s manufacturing facility in Gilbert, Arizona, performs final inspections of one Mission Extension Pod (MEP). Learn more Skip to content Login / Register Logout Shop Subscribe News Science Solar System Exoplanets Stars Milky Way Galaxies Exotic Objects Cosmology Observing In The Sky Upcoming Events The Sun The Moon Planets Comets Deep-Sky Objects Observing Basics Telescopes and Equipment Astrophotography Gear Guide This Week in Astronomy Space Exploration What’s Launching This Week Human Spaceflight Robotic Spaceflight The Magazine Ask Astro Star Products News Science Solar System Exoplanets Stars Milky Way Galaxies Exotic Objects Cosmology Observing In The Sky Upcoming Events The Sun The Moon Planets Comets Deep-Sky Objects Observing Basics Telescopes and Equipment Astrophotography Gear Guide This Week in Astronomy Space Exploration What’s Launching This Week Human Spaceflight Robotic Spaceflight The Magazine Ask Astro Star Products Login / Register Logout Shop Subscribe A robotic satellite servicer and Starship’s return headline this week’s launches Here's what's launching July 20–26: Northrop Grumman sends up its robotic satellite mechanic, SpaceX tries again for Starship Flight 13 after a last-second abort, and Falcon 9 keeps its Starlink cadence running. By Brooks Mendenhall | Published: July 20, 2026 The two robotic arms of Northrop Grumman's Mission Robotic Vehicle (MRV) are shown here at the U.S. Naval Research Laboratory during integration onto the spacecraft. Credit: Northrop Grumman, via U.S. Naval Research Laboratory, Public Domain Rocket launches this week On Tuesday, July 21 , SpaceX opens the week with the Starlink Group 17-39 mission , lifting off from Vandenberg Space Force Base at 10 a.m. EDT. The Falcon 9 booster is expected to land on the droneship Of Course I Still Love You in the Pacific Ocean. Watch it here . Later that afternoon at 5:15 p.m. EDT on Tuesday, July 21 , a Falcon 9 will lift off from Cape Canaveral Space Force Station carrying Northrop Grumman’s Mission Robotic Vehicle (MRV-1) and three Mission Extension Pods (MEPs). An evolution of the company’s Mission Extension Vehicles (MEVs), the MRV-1 is an on-orbit servicing spacecraft with the ability to inspect, repair, and upgrade satellites in geosynchronous orbit through the use of its robotic arms. It can also team up in orbit with independently launched MEPs — small jetpacks that attach to a satellite low on fuel — to extend the mission of satellites. MRV features a first-of-its kind standardized refueling port to ensure continued servicing of satellites for at least the next decade. Watch it here . Also on Tuesday, July 21 , at 10:50 p.m. EDT, Chinese firm Orienspace is scheduled to launch a Gravity 1 rocket from the Haiyang Oriental Spaceport carrying an undisclosed payload, according to tracking by Next Spaceflight . On Thursday, July 23 , at 8 a.m. EDT, a Long March 3B/E is set to lift off from Xichang Satellite Launch Center with an undisclosed payload, according to Next Spaceflight tracking. Later on Thursday, July 23 , SpaceX makes its second attempt at Starship Flight 13 , targeting a 90-minute window that opens at 6:45 p.m. EDT from Starbase, Texas. The company scrubbed its first try on July 16 after several Raptor 3 engines failed to ignite; two engines were replaced before this week’s attempt. Flight 13 aims to repeat the objectives from Flight 12 in May — deploying brand-new Starlink V3 satellites for the first time and relighting a Raptor engine in space — but this time hoping for a clean splashdown after the Super Heavy booster crashed into the Gulf of Mexico after a landing-burn engine issue on Flight 12. Starship’s continued success is critical to the Artemis program and NASA’s plan for a permanent lunar base. Also on Thursday, July 23 , at 7:30 p.m. EDT, Chinese commercial space launch provider CAS Space is scheduled to launch a Kinetica 1 rocket from Jiuquan Satellite Launch Center, again with an undisclosed payload per Next Spaceflight . Closing out the week on Friday, July 24 , at 10 a.m. EDT, SpaceX returns to Vandenberg for the Starlink Group 17-51 mission , with the booster targeting a landing on Of Course I Still Love You . Watch it here . Rocket launches last week Skyroot Aerospace’s Vikram-1 lifted off from the Satish Dhawan Space Centre on Saturday, July 18, at 2:35 a.m. EDT, becoming the first privately developed Indian rocket to reach orbit and making India the third country — after the United States and China — where a private company has pulled off an orbital launch. The four-stage rocket deployed its payloads roughly 17 minutes after liftoff, and mission control declared the debut, named Aagaman, a success. ORBIT ACHIEVED. 🚀 Vikram-1 Test Flight-1 has reached orbit. India's first privately developed orbital rocket has completed its final burn and injected its payloads into a ~450 km orbit, making India the third country in the world with private orbital launch capability.… — Skyroot Aerospace (@SkyrootA) July 18, 2026 SpaceX filled out the rest of the week. On Monday, July 13, a Falcon 9 launched the Starlink Group 15-14 mission from Vandenberg, landing its booster on Of Course I Still Love You . On Tuesday, July 14, SpaceX added the Starlink Group 10-45 mission from Cape Canaveral, with the booster landing on the droneship A Shortfall of Gravitas , while Roscosmos launched the Soyuz MS-29 crew mission to the International Space Station from Baikonur Cosmodrome. SpaceX closed the week on Thursday, July 16, with the Tranche 1 Transport Layer E mission for the Space Development Agency, launched from Vandenberg. Upcoming rocket launches On Monday, July 27, SpaceX is scheduled to launch the Starlink Group 17-52 mission from Vandenberg, with the booster again targeting Of Course I Still Love You . On Wednesday, July 29, a Long March 7A is expected to lift off from the Wenchang Space Launch Site carrying an undisclosed payload, per Next Spaceflight tracking. On Thursday, July 30, SpaceX is slated to launch NROL-95, a national security payload for the National Reconnaissance Office, from Cape Canaveral. Brooks Mendenhall is a staff writer for Astronomy magazine and is based in Chattanooga, Tennessee. records.excerpt: Title: SpaceX targets July 23 for crucial Starship Flight 13 test launch after abort URL Source: http://www.space.com/space-exploration/launches-spacecraft/spacex-targets-july-23-for-crucial-starship-flight-13-test-launch-after-abort Published Time: 2026-07-20T21:00:00+00:00 Markdown Content: ![Image 1: a giant rocket stands on a launch pad against a sunset sky](https://cdn.mos.cms.futurecdn.net/utXh7eg3hdTzfKujJxfqS3.jpg) SpaceX's Starship rocket stands on the pad ahead of its 13th test flight.(Image credit: SpaceX) SpaceX has pushed the next launch of its Starship megarocket back a few more days. [Elon Musk](https://www.space.com/18849-elon-musk.html)'s company is now targeting Thursday (July 23) for Flight 13 of [Starship,](https://www.space.com/spacex-starship-super-heavy.html) the giant, fully reusable vehicle it's developing to help get people to the moon and Mars, among other spaceflight tasks. If all goes to plan, the 408-foot-tall (124.4 meters) Starship will lift off from [SpaceX](https://www.space.com/18853-spacex.html)'s Starbase site in South Texas on Thursday during a 90-minute window that opens at 6:45 p.m. EDT (2245 GMT; 5:45 p.m. local Texas time). You can watch the action [live here at Space.com](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=bjAvEuIZDrA), courtesy of SpaceX. It will be the second launch attempt for [Starship Flight 13](https://www.space.com/space-exploration/launches-spacecraft/spacex-starship-flight-13-starlink-v3-satellites). The first came last Thursday (July 16) and [ended in an abort](https://www.space.com/space-exploration/launches-spacecraft/spacexs-starship-flight-13-test-launch-aborts-at-last-second-video), which occurred just as the giant rocket's 33 first-stage Raptor engines were firing up. "To be confident of a good flight, 2 Raptors will be removed & replaced. Most probable launch timing is early next week," Musk said on July 16 [via X](https://x.com/elonmusk/status/2077906757641183445), the social media platform he owns. SpaceX first targeted today (July 20) for Flight 13's second try. On Sunday (July 19), however, [the company announced](https://x.com/SpaceX/status/2078966109240262701) that it had pushed that date back to no earlier than Thursday. Flight 13 will be the second launch of Starship Version 3 (V3), the latest, most advanced iteration of the megarocket. V3 is the variant that will land astronauts on the moon for NASA's [Artemis program](https://www.space.com/artemis-program.html) and fly SpaceX's first Mars missions, if all goes to plan. The plan for the upcoming suborbital launch is similar to that of [Flight 12](https://www.space.com/space-exploration/launches-spacecraft/spacex-starship-v3-megarocket-first-test-flight), which lifted off on May 22. Starship's Super Heavy first stage will aim to steer itself back to Earth for a controlled splashdown in the Gulf of Mexico, while the Ship upper stage will do the same halfway around the world, off the coast of Western Australia. SpaceX accomplished the latter objective on Flight 12 but not the former; Super Heavy suffered engine issues during its return to Earth and ended up hitting the Gulf waters hard. Flight 13 will do a few new things, however. For example, it will carry 20 of SpaceX's next-gen [Starlink](https://www.space.com/spacex-starlink-satellites.html) V3 internet satellites, which have never flown to space before. SpaceX plans to build a constellation of [100,000 Starlink V3 spacecraft](https://www.space.com/space-exploration/satellites/spacex-wants-to-launch-100-000-starlink-satellites-to-orbit) in [low Earth orbit](https://www.space.com/low-earth-orbit) over the coming years, and Starship will do all of the heavy lifting. These 20 Starlinks won't stay aloft for long, however. Since Ship is flying on a suborbital trajectory, the satellites will come back to Earth relatively quickly — about 20 minutes after deployment, according to SpaceX's [Flight 13 mission description](https://www.spacex.com/launches/starship-flight-13). Starship debuted in April 2023. If you live in the Sunshine State, you know watching a rocket launch is such a Florida thing to do. That typically inspires people watching from the ground to whip out their phones and cameras to document liftoff, the rocket launch contrail and sometimes "[space jellyfish](https://www.floridatoday.com/story/tech/science/space/2026/07/14/space-jellyfish-florida-spacex-rocket-launch-effect-canaveral/90911398007/)." But we're not the only ones who documented this tremendous space coverage. Often, FLORIDA TODAY gets photo and video submissions from readers, too, ranging from rocket launch views along the Space Coast to Orlando and West Palm Beach. The content will be reviewed by an editor. Be sure to include your first and last name for credit purposes, the city and state where the event is happening and a brief description. Here is the direct link, [https://gannett-nxuao.formstack.com/forms/brevardugc](https://gannett-nxuao.formstack.com/forms/brevardugc). For questions or comments about rocket launch coverage from NASA's Kennedy Space Center or Cape Canaveral Space Force Station in Florida, email USA TODAY Network Space Reporters Rick Neale at rneale@floridatoday.com, Brooke Edwards at bedwards@floridatoday.com or Eric Lagatta at elagatta@usatoday.com. Here's the next Florida rocket launch for the week of July 20, 2026, and how to watch some [NASA content with Amazon Prime Video](https://www.primevideo.com/offers/nonprimehomepage/ref=dv_web_force_root?tag=usatlocal-20). * **Mission:** A SpaceX Falcon 9 rocket will launch Northrop Grumman's Mission Robotic Vehicle and Mission Extension Pod jetpacks. * **Launch window:**5:15 p.m. to 9:04 p.m. ET on Tuesday, July 21, 2026 * **Launch trajectory:**Due east * **Launch location:**Launch Complex 40 at Cape Canaveral Space Force Station near NASA's Kennedy Space Center in Florida * **Sonic booms for the Space Coast of Florida:**No * **Live coverage starts 90 minutes before liftoff at[floridatoday.com/space](http://www.floridatoday.com/space):**You can watch live rocket launch coverage from USA TODAY Network’s Space Team, which consists of FLORIDA TODAY space reporters Rick Neale and Brooke Edwards and visuals journalists Craig Bailey, Malcolm Denemark and Tim Shortt. Our Space Team will provide up-to-the-minute updates in a mobile-friendly live blog, complete with a countdown clock, at floridatoday.com/space, starting 90 minutes before liftoff. You can download the free FLORIDA TODAY app, which is available in the App Store or Google Play, or type**[floridatoday.com/space](http://www.floridatoday.com/space)**into your browser. ## Watch some rocket launches with NASA+ on Prime Video [Watch NASA+ content with Amazon Prime Video](https://www.primevideo.com/offers/nonprimehomepage/ref=dv_web_force_root?tag=usatlocal-20) NASA content, including some rocket launches, is available to watch on NASA+ on desktop, both[from its official site](https://plus.nasa.gov/)and[YouTube](https://www.youtube.com/NASA). The platform is also available to download as[a mobile app](https://www.nasa.gov/nasa-app/#:~:text=The%20redesigned%20NASA%20App%20unlocks,Install%20the%20NASA%20App%20today!)on smartphones. All NASA+ content is also available to those[who have Prime Video downloaded](https://www.primevideo.com/offers/nonprimehomepage/ref=dv_web_force_root?tag=usatlocal-20)on any of their devices – whether it be a smartphone or smart TV. The content, which does not require a Prime subscription to view, is one of Prime Video's FAST channels (free ad-supported television). records.excerpt:
SpaceX is preparing for its 13th Starship test flight. It was set to launch last Thursday, but at the last second, some of its engines did not start, triggering an automatic launch abort.

“They basically looked at all the first-stage-level engines and decided that all of them needed to be worked on," Don Platt said. "So, replacement or refurbishment is happening now.”

Don Platt is the director of Spaceport Education at Florida Tech, and Ken Kremer is a research chemist. Both say delays are par for the course, especially when testing a new rocket.

[related id='2f608498-7461-4b55-8265-49797b5f14fa' align='center' source=''][/related]

“This happens every day in spaceflight, so I don’t think it’s a big deal that they delay. What will be a big deal is if the rocket explodes and doesn’t accomplish what it’s supposed to do," Kremer said. "Having said that, they’re also under the gun to produce for NASA. They’ve got to get Starship up and running because that’s the human lander for NASA. If it doesn’t work, then SpaceX is out of the picture.”

[related id='9d872be0-e4a6-465d-b444-36db47922c84' align='center' source=''][/related]

“I think it’s critical that this is hopefully the last suborbital flight and that it’s a success because then that will set them up to do an orbital flight from Texas," Platt said. "If that can be done in the next couple of months, I suppose there is still the possibility of having a Starship launch from Florida before the end of the year.”

All of these milestones need to fall into place so Starship can be a part of the Artemis III integration test in low Earth orbit. That test is expected to help prepare the Starship system for its role in the Artemis IV mission.

The new launch date is Thursday at 6:45 p.m. EDT. The launch window is 90 minutes. However, weather in the Gulf could change that date.

records.excerpt: More than 900 million shares set to become eligible for tradingSpaceX (NASDAQ:SPCX) is preparing for one of the largest lock-up expirations in recent market... SpaceX lock-up expiry could release $116 billion worth of shares (NASDAQ:SPCX) Fiona Craig Wed, July 22, 2026 at 5:41 AM CDT 2 min read SPCX SpaceX Dragon capsule with Earth clouds ©NASA Johnson More than 900 million shares set to become eligible for trading SpaceX (NASDAQ:SPCX) is preparing for one of the largest lock-up expirations in recent market history, with approximately 911.5 million shares worth around $116 billion scheduled to become eligible for trading on August 6. The company confirmed on Tuesday that it will publish its second-quarter financial results on August 4, marking its first earnings report since listing on Wall Street. Two days later, lock-up restrictions affecting early investors, executives and other insiders will begin to expire. Under certain conditions, a further 455.8 million shares could also become available for trading. However, shares held by Elon Musk and a select group of insiders will remain locked until the middle of 2027. Alternative lock-up structure aims to limit market disruption While most newly listed companies impose a standard 180-day restriction on insider share sales following an initial public offering, SpaceX and its underwriting banks opted for a different approach because of the company's size and shareholder base. The structure was designed to increase the number of shares available to investors over time while seeking to avoid major disruptions to normal market supply and demand. Shares remain well below post-IPO highs SpaceX shares ended Tuesday's session 3% higher at $123.54, snapping a seven-session losing streak. Even after the rebound, the stock remains below its IPO price of $135. The shares have fallen nearly 50% from the intraday record of $225.64 reached on June 16 and are down 43% from the highest closing price of $211.39 recorded the same day. Wall Street sentiment remains broadly positive. Of the 33 analysts covering the company, 27 recommend either a strong buy or buy rating, while five suggest holding the stock and one recommends selling. The median price target stands at $226, implying approximately 77% upside from current levels. According to Forbes' Real-Time Billionaires Index, Elon Musk's estimated net worth stood at roughly $786 billion as of Tuesday, after exceeding $1 trillion on June 12. Starship test flight rescheduled for July 24 SpaceX has also confirmed a new launch date for the 13th suborbital test flight of Starship, which is now scheduled for July 24 at 00:45 Italian time from the company's Starbase facility in Texas. The previous launch attempt on July 17 was called off at liftoff after several Raptor engines failed to perform as expected. Musk later announced on social media platform X that the affected engines would be replaced. The upcoming mission is expected to evaluate a series of hardware and software upgrades across both stages of the launch system, including the Super Heavy booster and the Starship spacecraft, which is ultimately intended to carry astronauts on future missions. Mission objectives include completing every major phase of the flight successfully, including liftoff, ascent, stage separation, booster reentry and a controlled splashdown. records.excerpt: SpaceX Is Down 20%: Here's Why I'm Still Not Buying Oops, something went wrong Skip to navigation Skip to main content Skip to right column Yahoo Finance Sign in SpaceX Is Down 20%: Here's Why I'm Still Not Buying Adria Cimino, The Motley Fool Tue, July 21, 2026 at 7:25 PM CDT 3 min read SPCX NVDA Space Exploration Technologies (NASDAQ: SPCX) has drawn a great amount of excitement in recent times. The company, better known as SpaceX, completed the world's biggest initial public offering last month -- and saw its stock soar 27% in the first days of trading. In recent times, SpaceX stock has pulled back, even falling below its IPO price of $135. But even at this level, I think the stock is too expensive considering the risk involved -- that's why I'm still not buying. Let's check out the details. Missed Nvidia in 2009? This Rare Signal Is Flashing Again. In 2009, a "Double Down" signal flashed for a little-known chipmaker called Nvidia. For the first time in years, that same "Total Conviction" signal is flashing for a company 1/100th the size of Nvidia. Continue » Image source: Getty Images. A smart mix of businesses It's true that SpaceX offers a smart mix of growth businesses -- rocket launches, connectivity, and artificial intelligence (AI) -- and these businesses can work together to deliver efficiency. For example, SpaceX can use its rockets to deliver materials to space for the satellite-based internet service and the AI business . This offers SpaceX great autonomy and keeps costs down. The company has also made progress on goals such as bringing down the costs of rocket launches, and last year it completed more orbital launches than any other player. The connectivity business has seen its subscribers quadruple over three years, and this growth is key since this unit drives revenue growth. All of that is positive, and SpaceX, at $119 at the July 20 market close, is considerably lower than it was a few weeks ago. But I'm still not buying because the stock is expensive given the amount of risk involved. Prior to the IPO , Morningstar said its fair value for SpaceX was $63, which seems reasonable; today, the SpaceX price remains far from that level. Upcoming earnings reports I also think that before diving in, it's important to take a look at an earnings report or two to monitor the company's spending trends and the level of revenue that's being generated. So far, we may look at the financial picture over the past three years, as provided in the prospectus. But since SpaceX's capital expenditures are increasing, I'd like to see fresh earnings data. This is particularly key for a company like SpaceX, which has many goals linked to technologies that are still in development. For example, as SpaceX increases capital spending, is its revenue climbing at a fast pace? Last year, capex of $20 billion exceeded revenue, which was $18 billion. I'd like to see revenue step ahead in the coming quarters. At this point, SpaceX remains an interesting business that's made progress in key areas. The company could have a very bright future several years down the road, so I understand that some investors aim to get in early. But in my opinion, risk remains high, and visibility remains limited -- so even though SpaceX stock has declined, I'm still not buying. Should you buy stock in Space Exploration Technologies right now? records.excerpt: Tesla puts Starlink antenna in Cybercab | Electrek Skip to main content Go to the Electrek home page Tesla Tesla puts Starlink antenna in Cybercab Fred Lambert | Jul 20 2026 - 5:25 pm PT 59 Comments Tesla and Starlink say SpaceX’s satellite internet is now “directly integrated” into the Cybercab, Tesla’s dedicated robotaxi. The reveal came through a pair of posts on X on Monday, with a cutaway diagram showing a Starlink antenna sitting in the vehicle’s roof. Neither company explained why a car that drives itself on its own computer needs internet from space. What Tesla actually said Starlink posted the diagram with the line, “High-speed internet from space for the future of autonomous vehicles.” Tesla’s own post was shorter: “Starlink V5 directly integrated in Cybercab.” The graphic labels a “Starlink Integration” block in the roof, next to the camera and sensor callouts. Two questions: 1- can you clarify if this is in production right now? Cause your statement is unclear. 2- Why? — Fred Lambert (@FredLambert) July 20, 2026 That’s the whole announcement. No spec, no timeline, no explanation. Advertisement - scroll for more content And the timing raises an obvious question. Tesla is building the Cybercab before it can sell it or drive it itself , so “integrated in Cybercab” could mean a production feature or a rendering of a future plan. Tesla didn’t say which. Tesla’s own cars are built to not need a connection Here’s the part that makes the “internet from space” framing strange. Tesla’s self-driving system runs entirely on the car’s onboard computer — AI4 hardware in the Cybercab’s case. It perceives, plans, and drives without any data connection. That’s the core of Tesla’s whole approach. Cut the signal and the car keeps driving. Connectivity does other useful things: live routing and navigation, fleet dispatch, remote support for stuck vehicles, over-the-air updates, and streaming for passengers. All real. None of it is what keeps the car on the road. For that, satellite connectivity through Starlink could offer more coverage in some dead zones. But the catch is where the robotaxi actually operates. Tesla’s unsupervised service is limited to small geofenced zones in Austin, Houston, Dallas, and a tiny mapped area in Miami — dense metros that already have strong cellular coverage. Satellite’s advantage is filling gaps in rural and remote areas where cellular thins out. Tesla’s robotaxi is nowhere close to running there. So in every place a Cybercab would actually drive today, the satellite link solves a problem the car doesn’t have. The more likely explanation There’s a simpler read, and it fits a pattern. Musk keeps routing Tesla money and business toward his other companies. Tesla invested $2 billion in xAI, which SpaceX then absorbed in a mega-deal . We’ve laid out how a proposed Tesla-SpaceX tie-up would be Musk’s fourth billion-dollar self-deal . Top comment by Mrvc Liked by 6 people If you own a product / service, you use that product or service. That part isn't surprising. Starlink is in the process of economizing so more terminals also not surprising. A line sight network in product designed around cities isn't the smartest. Maybe they have a backup cellular modem. A starlink terminal with a built in cellular modem and plan that covers both could also be a product that would be useful to many. View all comments Bolting a Starlink terminal into every Cybercab is a subscription line for SpaceX, paid for by Tesla’s fleet. That’s a business reason. Electrek’s Take A robotaxi with no human aboard that loses its cellular link in a dead zone is a real problem, and a satellite fallback keeps the fleet from going dark. Redundancy for remote operation is a legitimate goal. But that goal is years away from mattering. Tesla is running a couple dozen cars in a handful of well-covered cities. It hasn’t earned the connectivity problem that Starlink would solve. Announcing a satellite integration now, for a car that isn’t in service and doesn’t need a connection to drive, is solving a problem Tesla doesn’t have yet while handing recurring revenue to another Musk company that does need the cash. When SpaceX ( NASDAQ: SPCX ) came to the market on 12 June via an Initial Public Offering (IPO), demand for the stock was sky-high. As a result, its share price soared. Yet since then, demand has cooled significantly, and to the surprise of many, the stock has actually fallen below its IPO price. With that in mind, here’s a look at how much £5,000 invested in the company immediately after the IPO would be worth today… Should you buy Space Exploration Technologies Corp. - Class A shares today? Before you decide, please take a moment to review this report first.
